Practice crop rotation with non leguminous plants such as tomato and cabbage every 3-4 seasons.
Plough deep to about 45cm to encourage rotting of the plant material.
Maintain weed-free fields to remove alternate host such as oxalis.
Avoid walking through the field during wet weather to prevent disease spread from one plant to another.
Work on healthy plants first then move to the infected area.
Uproot volunteer crops that could harbour the pathogen.
Monitoring: Look out for leaves with small orange/yellow, halo-like powdery pustules on the upper side and red, circular pustules on lower leaf surface.
Check for presence of pustules on petioles, pods and stem.
Look out for leaves that are dry and shrivelled which lead to defoliation.
Consider direct control actions when orange pustules are observed on leaves of 4-5 plants.
Direct Control: Remove and destroy old plants by burning.
WP at 1.25 g/L water every 2 weeks to one month depending on disease pressure.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
